claim: Let \(\mathcal L_{N,M}\) be the concrete quantum logic of a bipartite non-signalling box world with \(N\ge2\) binary-output inputs for Alice and \(M\ge2\) binary-output inputs for Bob, generated by the elementary events \([i,a;j,b]\). Every automorphism of the orthomodular poset \(\mathcal L_{N,M}\) is induced by permuting Alice's inputs, independently flipping the two outputs of each Alice input, permuting Bob's inputs, and independently flipping the two outputs of each Bob input; when \(N=M\), one may additionally interchange the two parties. Hence \[\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal L_{N,M})\cong (C_2\wr S_N)\times(C_2\wr S_M)\]for \(N\ne M\), while for \(N=M\) this product is extended by a \(C_2\) that swaps the two factors. In particular, \[|\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal L_{N,M})|=2^{N+M}N!M!\]when \(N\ne M\), and twice this number when \(N=M\). Thus the binary bipartite box logic has no hidden abstract symmetries beyond the standard operational relabelings.

correctness.rationale: Logic automorphisms preserve atoms and orthogonality. The closed non-orthogonality rectangle \((X\setminus\{\bar x\})\times(Y\setminus\{\bar y\})\) yields three exact intersection numbers that recover the rook coordinate relation. Maximal rook cliques recover rows and columns, up to a global party swap only for equal dimensions. The original orthogonality relation inside each row and column recovers the binary perfect matchings, leaving exactly \((C_2\wr S_N)\times(C_2\wr S_M)\) and the optional equal-size swap.

value.rationale: The result identifies the exact symmetry object needed to quotient finite box-world propositions, Bell-event structures, and symmetry-reduced computations. It proves operational relabelings are complete rather than merely obvious symmetries, rules out hidden logical identifications, and gives a closed group/order formula for every binary bipartite input size with \(N,M\ge2\).
